transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
We're expecting to hear from President Trump shortly about what's come out of his historic
trilateral summit in Shenzhen with the leaders of China and Russia on the sidelines of the
APEC summit.
There were no known breakthroughs on nuclear control, AI, or Russia's war with Ukraine,
but covering the talks from Jakarta, Nina Rao says the trip produced billions of dollars
in economic deals.
The White House says the commercial and defense agreements total more than $17 billion across
the region.
It includes a $12 billion agreement with the Philippines flagship carrier, Philippine Airlines,
to buy up to 20 Boeing 787 jets.
The U.S. is also pursuing a $2 billion military financing loan package with Manila.
Washington substantially concluded a trade deal with Thailand that cuts tariffs on 99%
of goods and announced energy and tech investments in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei.
For NPR News, I'm Nina Rao in Jakarta.
Enthropic shares are down more than 11% after the artificial intelligence powerhouse capped
its first day of trading on the NASDAQ with a market value of $1.75 trillion.
The company founded five years ago by open AI defectors began trading yesterday under
the ticker symbol ANT with a blockbuster IPO that surpassed the record set by SpaceX.
Enthropic stock opened at $111.50 a share on Thursday.
This hour, the price is down to roughly $85.72.
California Attorney General Rob Bonta has served the chipmaker NVIDIA with an investigative
subpoena.
Here's NPR's John Ruich.
The California AG's office says in a statement it's asking NVIDIA whether its advanced chips
or confidential information may have gone to China and whether NVIDIA misled investors
and the public.
Bonta says the conduct of the company and former CEO Jensen Huang raises red flags.
Huang stepped down last week after admitting to an extramarital affair.
U.S. intelligence services believe one of the women had ties to a Chinese spy agency.
Huang had been a vocal opponent of U.S. export controls that banned certain high-end chips
from being exported to China.
John Ruich, NPR News.
New psychedelic treatments could become more widely available as soon as next year, here's
NPR's Will Stone.
Studies on psychedelics screen patients carefully beforehand and monitor them closely while they're
under the influence.
However, a minority of patients do experience new and sometimes serious difficulties in the
weeks and months after.
Research suggests serious adverse events like suicidality are very rare in drug trials.
Experts like Roman Politsky at Emory University School of Medicine, who's running a study
on this, says it isn't being tracked well enough and the full array of problems aren't
being documented.
Quite common on the list are things like anxiety, depression.
Will Stone with the story, it's NPR News.
Israel has carried out airstrikes in eastern Lebanon's Bekha Valley for the second time
and BR's Jawad Raskala has more from Beirut.
Lebanese state media say Israeli warplanes carried out five airstrikes Thursday evening
near the town of Janta and the Bekha Valley, close to the Syrian border.
The Israeli military says it struck the entrances to a site previously used by Iran-backed Hezbollah
to make missiles and store weapons, to prevent it from being restored.
Israel also struck the same area on Monday, saying it was targeting a weapons shipment
destined for Hezbollah.
Israeli strikes in the Bekha have become much less frequent since a US-Iran agreement in
June led to a reduction in the scope of airstrikes.
Israel had been hitting the region much more regularly earlier this year, but in southern
Lebanon Israeli attacks continue daily, according to Lebanese state media.
Jawad Raskala, NPR News, Beirut.
Congressman Jamie Raskin, the lawmaker widely expected to be named chair of the powerful
House Judiciary Committee when Democrats take control of Congress in January, is advising
Trump administration officials to preserve all records.
The incoming majority leadership has warned that it's prepared to hold investigations
into public corruption, a top concern for many voters, as they decided midterm races
this month.
The National Weather Service is posting flood warnings and watches in Florida along a 200-mile
stretch from Melbourne to Jacksonville.
Areas further south have received more than 17 inches of rain along the Atlantic coast.
Dozens of people had to be rescued this week.
On the west coast, rescues, floods and mudslides were also reported this week in southern California.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump's trilateral summit in Shenzhen with China and Russia leaders yields no major breakthroughs
Trump administration touts over $17 billion in regional deals, including $12 billion Philippine Airlines Boeing order
Anthropic shares fall over 11% after first day of NASDAQ trading at $1.75 trillion valuation
California Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenas NVIDIA over possible chip exports to China
Psychedelic treatments could become more widely available next year, with adverse effects poorly tracked
Israel conducts second round of airstrikes in Lebanon's Bekaa Valley targeting Hezbollah missile sites
Jamie Raskin advises Trump administration to preserve records ahead of Democratic House investigations
National Weather Service issues flood warnings in Florida from Melbourne to Jacksonville after heavy rain
